archive_context.text: Consequence design is really part-speculative, part sci-fi -- trying to imagine a better future state, instead of allowing constraints to limit what's possible from the outset. Some of that is reframing "edge cases" as "people on the margins" https://twitter.com/zeldman/status/1285346647757787142

The last thing the world needs is another Robin Hood take, but there's a set of retro/post-mortems to be held about what happens when we lure users to cauldron to turn them into soup when the wolves get hungry.
I mean, the tone/voice & emojis for when someone makes a trade versus whatever PR-speak got mailed to users after their trust was broken is...a stark contrast.

What's the designer's role in all this shenanigans? Depends on where you sit, I guess. I'm just as mad about really terrible supermarket kiosks as I am about gamified stock UIs, though. There's a reckoning necessary & a whole new set of roles we have yet to imagine to fix this.
Wrote a few weeks ago about the ways we hide the real cost of experiences by throwing a UI layer between stuff we used to do for ourselves. https://consequencedesign.org/docs/who-pays-this-person/

Part of the reason it's taken me so long to write (besides procrastination & a pandemic) is the realization halfway through that I wasn't writing a "design" book, but a policy book. Consequence Design is a stance.

archive_context.text: More than half the NFL teams are still family owned businesses. Also, it's annoyed me for years that all of the major sports in the US are all from the 19th century.

Ultimate is the only modern sport so far to really break through and that took decades before states started sanctioning that as a HS sport. Adults professionalizing youth sports took a lot of the wind out of the sails of organic sports catching on.

Also, most would-be sport designers try to monetize their creation and never do enough play testing. 

I'm almost 18 years into accidentally creating a sport & the core elements work but you're always tweaking and refining the rules, but only because I can conjure up new players.
